content.prompt: The diagonals of a square $ABCD$ are $AC$ and $BD$, which intersect at $O$. The bisector of $\angle BAC$ cuts $BO$ at $X$ and $BC$ at $Y$. Prove that $CY=2OX$. (Hint: Let $AY$ meet $CD$ at $Z$ and consider $\triangle ACZ$.)

answer.worked: Extend AY to meet CD produced at Z. Put $\angle BAY=\alpha$. Since AY bisects BAC, $\angle YAC=\alpha$. As $BA\parallel CZ$, alternate angles give $\angle AZC=\alpha$. Hence $\triangle ACZ$ is isosceles, so $CZ=CA=2OA$ because the diagonals of a square bisect one another. The diagonals are perpendicular, so $\angle AOX=90^\circ=\angle ZCY$. Also $\angle OAX=\angle CZY=\alpha$. Therefore $\triangle AOX\sim\triangle ZCY$ by AAA. Corresponding side ratios give $\frac{CY}{OX}=\frac{CZ}{OA}=2$, so $CY=2OX$.
